configuration: Initial Alpha-Service runtime described in Section 3 of arXiv 2510.14359v1: an Input Unit with a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B trigger model and a Qwen2.5-VL-7B streaming model on first-person AI-glasses video, a Qwen3-8B Orchestrator LLM as the Central Processing Unit doing task dispatch and synthesis, an Arithmetic Logic Unit doing web search via the Google Search API, a local JSON-based Memory Unit (the paper's 'initial implementation'), and a pyttsx3 text-to-speech Output Unit, demonstrated in three qualitative case studies (Blackjack guide, museum tour, fit advisor) on Xiaomi AI glasses.
sources_read: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.14359v1 (paper, version 2510.14359v1): Abstract, Section 1 Introduction, Sections 2.1-2.3, Sections 3.1-3.6, Section 4 Case Study with Figure 1-5 captions, Section 6 Challenges, Section 7 Conclusion; read through the WebFetch summarizing tool, so all quotes are labeled UNVERIFIED
cases/alpha-service/case.yaml and README.md (case metadata only; the listed sha256 could not be checked because direct download was not permitted in this session)
No code repository exists for this work; judged from the paper text alone

S->M.label: reported
S->M.rationale: Section 3.5 describes an implemented write path: after each interaction the system extracts key information from the dialogue (which carries the user's input and the conversation context) and stores it asynchronously as a JSON memory record whose fields include user metadata and a concise summary of the dialogue history. This is user-supplied and sensed evidence admitted to a cross-session store, not a static benchmark profile.
S->M.locator: Section 3.5 Memory Unit: Long-Term Context Storage, record-fields sentence and write-operation sentences (sentences 6, 8, 9 of the section)
S->M.quote: UNVERIFIED: "After each interaction, the system automatically extracts key information from the dialogue and stores it in a structured JSON record." ... "Each memory record captures a single interaction episode and contains the following fields: user metadata (e.g., ID, role), a concise summary of the dialogue history, the agent's final output, a unique timestamp, and a high-level topic tag automatically generated by the agent."

M->A.label: reported
M->A.rationale: Retained interaction records are searched at task initiation and injected into the Orchestrator LLM's prompt, and the CPU's synthesis phase integrates relevant past interactions from the Memory Unit into the final answer. The CPU also explicitly routes a sub-task to the Memory Unit for retrieval. That is retained information delivered to the Action decision about response content.
M->A.locator: Section 3.5 Memory Unit, retrieval sentences (sentences 10-12); Section 3.3 Central Processing Unit, Decomposition and Dispatch routing item 5 and Synthesis and Response Generation paragraph
M->A.quote: UNVERIFIED: "When a new task is initiated, the agent parses the current query to identify its topic or intent, and then searches the memory for relevant past entries. Retrieved context is selectively injected into the language model's prompt, enabling continuity across sessions and improving the model's grounding and response relevance." ... "it may receive a detailed visual description from the video LLM, search results from the ALU, and relevant past interactions from the Memory Unit."

A->S.label: reported
A->S.rationale: The Orchestrator LLM (Action) decomposes the request into sub-tasks and routes some of them back to the perception models: it activates the trigger model to watch for the optimal timing of a response planned for a future time step, and invokes the streaming video LLM to produce task-specific visual descriptions when it needs finer-grained information. Action's plans and information needs therefore set Sensing targets, acquisition, and interpretation. This is an in-system flow, not an external grader.
A->S.locator: Section 3.3 Central Processing Unit, Decomposition and Dispatch routing list, items 2 and 3
A->S.quote: UNVERIFIED: "Activation of a trigger model to identify the optimal timing for responses required at a designated future time step." ... "Invocation of a streaming video LLM to produce detailed, task-specific visual descriptions when finer-grained information is necessary."

M->S.label: insufficient
M->S.rationale: No passage describes retained information reaching the Input Unit, trigger model, or streaming model; the only described inputs to perception are the glasses video stream and user command/intent cues. Memory is read only at task initiation into the language model's prompt, which is M->A. The CPU may both retrieve memory and dispatch the perception models, but that is at most the composition M->A->S, which does not establish M->S. The Introduction's aspiration that long-term memory lets the system continuously learn user habits names no sensing-side use. The paper does not explicitly exclude the route either, so the link is unknown rather than absent.
M->S.locator: Section 3.2 Input Unit: Trigger and Streaming MLLMs (no memory input described); Section 3.5 Memory Unit, retrieval sentences 10-11; Section 1 Introduction
M->S.quote: UNVERIFIED: "The first component is a lightweight, continuously-running 'trigger' model, a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B [5], which directly processes the video stream from the agent's first-person perspective glasses." ... "We designed an efficient 'user command + intent' dual-trigger mechanism, where this online model continuously analyzes incoming data for user assistance cues."

A->M.label: reported
A->M.rationale: Each JSON memory record stores the agent's final output and an agent-generated topic tag, written automatically by the system after each interaction, and the stated purpose is to let the agent recall past queries, actions, and preferences. The assistant's utterance and action record are therefore delivered to Memory by the service itself, not merely observed through Sensing.
A->M.quote: UNVERIFIED: "This allows the agent to recall past queries, actions, and preferences, thereby improving continuity and service quality in dynamic environments." ... "the agent's final output, a unique timestamp, and a high-level topic tag automatically generated by the agent."

record.label: stated
record.rationale: The service itself writes, after every interaction, a persistent JSON record containing its own final output together with the dialogue summary, timestamp, and topic tag, and later sessions retrieve these records. These are the service's own records kept for later use, not author-only trial logs.
record.quote: UNVERIFIED: "Each memory record captures a single interaction episode and contains the following fields: user metadata (e.g., ID, role), a concise summary of the dialogue history, the agent's final output, a unique timestamp, and a high-level topic tag automatically generated by the agent." ... "After each interaction, the system automatically extracts key information from the dialogue and stores it in a structured JSON record."

outcome.label: not_stated
outcome.rationale: No mechanism obtains or retains later evidence about the agent's actions (reply, rating, dismissal, correction, or observed result). User feedback and correction are placed explicitly in the future in the Challenges section, and the three case studies report no feedback collection, outcome tracking, or quantitative evaluation.
outcome.locator: Section 6 Challenges, 'User Adaptation and Trust Building' paragraph; Section 4 Case Study (Figures 3-5); Section 3.5 Memory Unit
outcome.quote: UNVERIFIED: "The system should have an explainable decision-making mechanism in the future and allow users to provide feedback, correct inaccuracies, or disable services during interactions, thereby gradually building trust and promoting human-AI collaboration."

attribution.label: not_stated
attribution.rationale: Nothing links an outcome to the decision it concerns or uses it to check or correct assistance. The only conflict resolution described is the Orchestrator reconciling its input sources (visual description, search results, past interactions) while composing a single answer, which is integration of inputs rather than evaluation of a prior action.
attribution.locator: Section 3.3 Synthesis and Response Generation paragraph; Section 3.5 Memory Unit; Section 6 Challenges
attribution.quote: UNVERIFIED: "The Orchestrator LLM then integrates these disparate pieces of information, resolves any potential conflicts, and synthesizes them into a single, context-aware, and comprehensive answer."

revision.label: not_stated
revision.rationale: The only durable write is appending interaction-episode content to a JSON store that a fixed retrieval-augmented prompting mechanism consumes; that is content used by a fixed mechanism, not a reusable rule, prompt, skill, code, or parameter change made by the service. The fine-tuning of the Qwen2.5-VL-3B trigger model and the Qwen3-8B orchestrator was done by the authors offline. The Introduction's reference to the self-evolution properties of agent systems is a general aspiration with no described mechanism, and the Conclusion lists improving the Memory Unit as future work.
revision.locator: Section 3.5 Memory Unit (sentences 5, 8, 11-12); Section 1 Introduction; Section 3.2 and 3.3 (author fine-tuned models); Section 7 Conclusion
revision.quote: UNVERIFIED: "This retrieval-augmented prompting strategy enhances the agent's ability to recall prior knowledge and adapt to user-specific patterns over time." ... "the system should not require pre-definition or specialized training for every task, but instead rely on the inherent strong generalization capabilities of large models and the self-evolution properties of agent systems."
revision.what: None. The only persistent change is new JSON interaction records (user metadata, dialogue summary, agent output, timestamp, topic tag), which are content for the fixed retrieval mechanism, not a revised mechanism.

later_use.label: not_stated
later_use.rationale: No revised mechanism exists, so no later run under one is reported. The case studies are three qualitative demonstrations that do not even report the Memory Unit being exercised across sessions, and the Conclusion defers Memory Unit personalization and user studies to future research.
later_use.locator: Section 4 Case Study (Figures 3-5 captions); Section 7 Conclusion
later_use.quote: UNVERIFIED: "In future research, we plan to enhance the personalization capacity of the Memory Unit, broaden the toolset of the Arithmetic Logic Unit, and conduct large-scale user studies to assess the long-term impact of proactive assistance in everyday contexts."

notes: Judged the initial Alpha-Service runtime of Section 3 in arXiv 2510.14359v1 (trigger/streaming MLLM Input Unit, Qwen3-8B Orchestrator CPU with task dispatch and synthesis, Google-Search ALU, local JSON Memory Unit described as the 'initial implementation', pyttsx3 Output Unit), as demonstrated in Section 4's three case studies on Xiaomi AI glasses. No code repository exists, so the paper text is the only evidence. The paper was read only through the WebFetch summarizing tool because direct download was not permitted in this session; every quote is therefore labeled UNVERIFIED, although the Section 3.5 memory sentences and the Section 3.3 routing list were returned with identical wording by independent fetches. The case file's sha256 could not be checked. Memory writes and reads are described as working paths (S->M, A->M, M->A) and the CPU's dispatch to the trigger and streaming models gives A->S, but nothing describes memory guiding perception, and no outcome feedback, attribution, or self-revision mechanism exists; the authors list feedback, explainability, and Memory Unit personalization as future work.
